title: Sub-Scope Document Editing Delivery
summary: supply an explicit parent or sub-scope document target to the existing source and metadata editors while keeping the public manifest minimal
content_html:
Sub-Scope Document Editing Delivery

Complete Result

On a configured sub-scope report, the ordinary Source action edits the parent report document and a separate subdoc Source action edits the currently displayed, validated sub-scope document.

The existing Edit metadata action edits the current rendered target: the parent report on its list view or the validated sub-scope document on its detail view. The sub-scope modal retains every existing editable field except Parent, including non-viewable.

The manage report lists every sub-scope document and shows the existing Status and non-viewable icons from a compact management-only inventory. The public report continues to receive only its minimal public manifest and shows neither icon.

Both Source actions supply an explicit target. The existing Markdown source editor never derives its target from the displayed document. Source mode has an explicit Return to doc action instead of using either Source action as a toggle.

Control-state contract

Rendered report list:

  • Edit metadata supplies the parent report target;
  • parent report Source is enabled;
  • subdoc Source is disabled; and
  • Return to doc is unavailable.

Rendered valid subdoc detail:

  • Edit metadata supplies the validated sub-scope target;
  • parent report Source remains enabled and supplies the parent doc_id;
  • subdoc Source is enabled and supplies the configured sub_scope and displayed subdoc; and
  • Return to doc is unavailable.

Markdown source:

  • Edit metadata is unavailable;
  • both source-entry actions are visible and disabled;
  • Return to doc is enabled;
  • Save/Rebuild and all existing registered source-editor actions keep their current availability rules; and
  • the toolbar does not permit switching source targets inside a dirty editor.

An unknown, unlisted, loading, or failed subdoc never enables subdoc Source or targets Edit metadata. The report announces valid rendered-detail state through an explicit management integration boundary; toolbar code does not infer validity by scraping report markup or trusting the URL parameter alone.

Explicit managed document target

Source mode and Edit metadata each receive exactly one required target:

parent target:    { scope, doc_id }
sub-scope target: { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }

Neither workflow falls back to selected-document state, displayed payload, doc, or subdoc. Ordinary non-report editing also supplies its target explicitly.

The source target remains fixed for the mounted editor session. Read, rebuild, and Open in VS Code use it. Add image, Add file, Add catalogue token, token inspection/editing, and future registered contributions act through the same active editor context rather than resolving another document.

Edit metadata loads the full record through the local management service using the supplied target. It does not hydrate from the minimal public manifest or compact public by-ID payload.

Public and manage list data remain separate. Public mode receives publicly eligible { doc_id, title } records. Manage mode receives all sub-scope documents with doc_id, title, ui_status, and viewable in one local inventory rather than issuing one by-ID request per row.

Route and return behavior

Entering either source action does not rewrite the document route. For example, editing the subdoc at:

/docs/?scope=analysis&doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=d-20260624-204534-0d6ae2

preserves both doc and subdoc.

Successful Save/Rebuild retains the current source-editor behavior of returning to rendered view. Return to doc requests the same rendered mode without changing the route and reuses the existing unsaved-change prompt. Browser Back/Forward continues to own report detail state, not source target state.

Opening or saving Edit metadata also preserves the route. A successful subdoc metadata save refreshes the displayed detail and the manifest row when an existing manifest field changes, without selecting the subdoc in the parent index.

Service and rebuild boundary

  • Source read, rebuild, and open requests accept optional sub_scope alongside scope and doc_id.
  • Metadata read and POST /docs/update-metadata accept the same explicit target.
  • An absent sub_scope preserves the current parent-scope behavior exactly.
  • A present sub_scope must identify a configured one-level child of scope; the service resolves only that child document root.
  • The requested doc_id must exist in that sub-scope and match its source front matter.
  • Rebuild preserves the current revision, timestamp, atomic-write, suppression, diagnostics, and activity contracts while invoking the targeted sub-scope document and search builders.
  • The sub-scope metadata request supports Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and viewable. It omits parent_id; the service rejects that field for a sub-scope target and never introduces or changes sub-scope parentage.
  • Metadata hydration reads full source front matter locally. It does not expand the public manifest beyond its existing minimal record contract.
  • The local management inventory includes all sub-scope documents and the two fields required for existing Status/non-viewable icons. It is not copied to the public projection.
  • A viewable change retains the existing visibility contract and refreshes the local management inventory and public eligibility without adding viewable to public manifest rows.
  • Successful subdoc rebuild refreshes the by-ID detail payload and remounts the report detail without changing parent index selection.
  • Invalid or unavailable targets fail before source access and leave rendered state recoverable.

In Scope

  • Add the subdoc Source and Return to doc toolbar controls.
  • Convert the current Source control from a rendered/source toggle into a one-way explicit-target entry action.
  • Project the exact control states above.
  • Let the mounted report publish validated subdoc detail state to the management layer through a narrow callback or event contract.
  • Supply explicit targets to both editing workflows and retain the source target for one editor session.
  • Make the existing Edit metadata action target the parent report on list view and the displayed subdoc on a validated detail view.
  • Hydrate a full sub-scope source record without projecting management metadata into public payloads.
  • Supply one compact manage-only inventory containing all identities, ui_status, and viewable, and render the existing Status/non-viewable icons in manage report rows.
  • Present the existing metadata modal without Parent for a sub-scope target, while preserving Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and non-viewable.
  • Extend metadata mutation and targeted reload behavior for optional sub_scope.
  • Extend the source client, adapter, resolver, rebuild, open-source, activity, and rendered-refresh boundaries for optional sub_scope.
  • Preserve all current source-editor controls and contribution contracts.
  • Add focused service, control-state, module-integration, and route/request evidence.

Not In Scope

  • Changing the public report UI or exposing source controls publicly.
  • Selecting sub-scope documents in the parent index.
  • A second editor, reduced subdoc editor, or report-owned write form.
  • Sub-scope document create, delete, move, transfer, Recent, or global search adoption.
  • Encoding source mode or source target as a new URL parameter.
  • Changing semantic-token syntax or Catalogue target behavior.
  • Publishing or rendering subdoc ui_status; that remains the separate low-priority detail-header enhancement recorded by the parent feature.

Confirmed Authority

  • The new browser target normalizer belongs in one focused management module, docs-viewer-management-document-target.js. Source and metadata entry use its exact allowlisted shape; neither workflow owns a second normalizer.
  • The new server resolver belongs in docs_management_document_target.py. Source reads/rebuilds/open, metadata reads/mutations, and the management inventory consume that resolver rather than retaining service-local lookup variants.
  • site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-report.js is the only owner that can validate a displayed subdoc. It knows the configured sub-scope, list membership, requested ID, by-ID request state, and loaded payload identity. It publishes or clears an optional management callback only after those checks; management code does not scrape its DOM.
  • docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-document-reports.js is the manage-only bridge that supplies inventory and receives validated report state. docs-viewer-reports.js remains the shared read-only loader and the public caller supplies neither management input nor callback.
  • docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/source-editor/source-editor.js owns the fixed mounted source target. Its current docId state and selected-document update() comparison are replaced by one immutable normalized target; the source adapter, contextual contributions, and source-file actions consume that mounted context.
  • site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-app-runtime.js owns return to rendered content through sourceEditorServices.reloadRenderedDoc and reloadGeneratedDoc. For a sub-scope target it remounts the still-selected parent report without rewriting the route; the sub-scope report then owns re-fetching and rendering the preserved subdoc.
  • Toolbar registration/projection remains in docs-viewer-management-hosted-views.js, docs-viewer-management-control-renderers.js, and docs-viewer-management.js; action dispatch remains in docs-viewer-management-actions.js.
  • Metadata orchestration remains in docs-viewer-management-metadata-workflow.js, docs-viewer-management-modals.js, and docs-viewer-management-modal-composition.js. Full target-aware hydration moves to the local management client/read service and no longer uses loadManagedDocumentRecord over the selected generated payload.
  • Service routing remains in docs_management_routes.py, docs_management_read_service.py, docs_management_service.py, and docs_management_mutation_service.py. Source behavior remains in docs_management_source_service.py; metadata planning remains in docs_management_mutations.py; write/rebuild mechanics remain in docs_write_rebuild.py.
  • Configured child roots remain owned by docs_scope_config.py; sub-scope document/public-manifest generation remains owned by docs_builder/sub_scope.py, build_docs.py, and build_search.py. docs_publish_gate.py is verification coverage, not an implementation owner for the management inventory or editor target.

Delivery Tracker

Current state: in progress. SDE-0 through SDE-4 are complete. The mounted report publishes only validated detail state, the manage bridge supplies one local inventory, and toolbar availability/targets come from one pure control projection. SDE-5 and SDE-6 have not started.

Next checkpoint: review SDE-4. Do not start SDE-5 without approval.

Review rule: complete one phase, record its evidence beneath that phase, and stop for review before starting the next phase. A passing sample proves only the named boundary; it does not advance later phases automatically.

[x] SDE-0 — Freeze The Explicit-Target Contract And Authority Map

  • [x] Trace the current rendered/source toggle, selected-document fallback, Edit metadata hydration/save, report-detail state, and rendered reload paths from their UI controls to their service owners.
  • [x] Record one normalized target shape used by both editing workflows: { scope, doc_id } for a parent document and { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } for a configured sub-scope document.
  • [x] Identify the single owner that validates a displayed subdoc, the single owner that retains the mounted source target, and the single owner that remounts rendered detail after a targeted rebuild.
  • [x] Add pure contract fixtures for parent, valid sub-scope, unlisted subdoc, unknown sub-scope, mismatched front-matter identity, loading, and failed detail states.
  • [x] Capture focused baseline evidence for ordinary parent source editing, metadata editing, dirty return, stale revision, source-editor contributions, public sub-scope manifest shape, and report navigation.
  • [x] Confirm the maintained files and lowest stable tests for every later phase; revise Confirmed Authority where inspection disproves a starting point.

SDE-0 trace and decisions

  • Source currently travels from the registered markdown-source toolbar control through the action resolver's active selected document, toggles document mode, then lets source-editor.js read context.selectedDoc. The source adapter passes a bare doc_id; the client injects ambient scope; docs_management_source_service.py performs its own parent-scope lookup.
  • Edit metadata currently resolves the active selected document, hydrates from the generated payload cache/collection provider through loadManagedDocumentRecord, always renders Parent, posts a parent mutation, and reloads the parent index.
  • docs-subscope-report.js alone loads the manifest, rejects an unlisted URL subdoc, fetches the by-ID payload, and renders list/detail/error state. It does not currently publish management state or verify the loaded payload's doc_id; both checks belong at this owner in SDE-4.
  • reloadGeneratedDoc clears generated caches, preserves current report route parameters through the route workflow, reloads the parent index, and thereby remounts report detail. The report module, not the reload service, owns the subsequent by-ID detail fetch/render.
  • The current dirty-leave prompt is not a Cancel-stays contract. beforeLeave blocks the first mode switch; Yes rebuilds, while No discards the buffer and returns to the rendered parent. SDE-5 reuses the dirty detector and modal shell but intentionally adds the settled Cancel-keeps-session behavior.
  • At the SDE-0 checkpoint, read_source_body accepted doc as an alias for doc_id. SDE-1 removed that unjustified alias when it routed source reads through the exact target resolver.

The shared fixture docs-viewer/tests/fixtures/docs_managed_document_targets_v1.json separates syntactic normalization, server resolution, and validated rendered-detail state. A successfully loaded report target can still fail server resolution for mismatched source front matter; loading, failed, unlisted, and unknown states never fall back to the parent for Edit metadata or subdoc Source.

SDE-2 test_docs_management_source_service.py; test_docs_write_rebuild.py; docs_viewer_catalogue_token_modules.py; focused source client/adapter module coverage
SDE-3 test_docs_management_mutations.py; test_docs_management_metadata.py; focused metadata client/workflow/modal module coverage
SDE-4 fixture-driven pure control projection and docs_subscope report-module coverage; public_docs_viewer_readonly.py for the unchanged public surface

SDE-0 evidence

  • pytest over the new fixture contract, parent source service, metadata mutation planner, and metadata service: 27 passed.
  • pytest over the sub-scope builder plus sub-scope search exclusion: 4 passed. This proves only the existing minimal manifest and exclusion contracts named by those tests.
  • docs_viewer_catalogue_token_modules.py --site-root .: passed. The active source adapter, stale captured-range guard, Catalogue action, and contextual Info contribution remain available.
  • One temporary browser probe of the current dirty editor: beforeLeave returned false; the prompt exposed No/Yes; choosing No requested rendered-document and reload:parent-report.
  • public_docs_viewer_readonly.py --site-root site: passed. Its Analysis sub-scope slice covered the minimal manifest, listed detail, missing detail, Back/Forward, explicit Back, stable parent selection, and absence of manage runtime on the public route.
  • The maintained docs_viewer_service_manage.py smoke could not supply additional route evidence because an independent Document Package baseline failed first: PayloadBuilderMixin.item_entry() received five positional arguments although its current signature accepts four. This delivery did not change or mask that separate defect; the focused green parent source and metadata evidence above is the SDE-0 baseline. The Document Package defect was repaired separately before SDE-1.

Checkpoint / review gate: no runtime behavior changes. Review the exact target normalizer/resolver owner, report-to-management integration seam, rendered-detail reload owner, maintained test list, and green parent-behavior baseline before SDE-1.

[x] SDE-1 — Add Managed Target Resolution And Inventory

  • [x] Add one server-side managed-document target resolver that accepts the two approved shapes and returns a confined source document plus its parent scope and optional configured sub-scope.
  • [x] Preserve current parent resolution when sub_scope is absent. When it is present, require a configured one-level child, resolve only that child's source root, require the requested source file, and verify front-matter doc_id.
  • [x] Reject blank, unknown, unlisted, mismatched, nested, or path-escaping targets before source read or mutation.
  • [x] Remove the source-read doc query alias; exact managed source requests use doc_id and no compatibility target name.
  • [x] Add one compact management-only sub-scope inventory containing every configured sub-scope document, including non-viewable records, with exactly doc_id, title, ui_status, and viewable.
  • [x] Keep the public manifest restricted to publicly eligible { doc_id, title } records and keep compact public by-ID payloads unchanged.
  • [x] Add focused resolver, confinement, inventory, and public-projection tests for repository and external-local source roots.

SDE-1 implementation and evidence

  • docs_management_document_target.py owns both approved target shapes, configured one-level sub-scope lookup, direct-child confinement, source identity verification, and the source-backed management inventory. Parent targets retain the existing front-matter identity lookup even when a source filename differs.
  • GET /docs/sub-scope-documents returns every configured sub-scope document, including non-viewable records, with only the four approved record fields. Repository and external-local scopes use the same configured-root resolver.
  • GET /docs/source now requires doc_id, accepts optional sub_scope, and uses the shared resolver. Rebuild and Open in VS Code remain on their existing parent-only paths until SDE-2.
  • The working sub-scope build keeps all by-ID payloads for local management but restricts its manifest to viewable { doc_id, title } rows. The public publish projection uses that manifest membership to exclude hidden by-ID files while copying eligible payload bytes unchanged. Parent index, Recent, and global search behavior is unchanged.
  • Focused pytest over the frozen fixture, resolver/inventory, source service, management routes, scope config, sub-scope builder, search exclusion, and publish gate: 66 passed.
  • Maintained explicit Python lint over the eleven changed Python source/test files: passed. git diff --check: passed.

Checkpoint / review gate: direct service evidence proves valid parent and sub-scope resolution, every invalid-target rejection, complete manage inventory, and byte-equivalent public payload shapes. No source or metadata UI is wired before review.

[x] SDE-2 — Make Source Editing Target-Aware

  • [x] Change the source client and adapter to accept one explicit target rather than a bare doc_id plus ambient scope; include sub_scope in source read, rebuild, and Open in VS Code requests only for a sub-scope target.
  • [x] Mount the approved target once in source-editor state and use it for the complete session. Remove selected, active, displayed, URL doc, and URL subdoc fallbacks from source entry and source-file actions.
  • [x] Extend source read, source rebuild, and open-source services through the shared managed target resolver.
  • [x] Route a sub-scope Save/Rebuild through the configured sub-scope document and search builders while preserving atomic write, source revision, timestamp, suppression, diagnostics, and activity contracts.
  • [x] Keep Add image, Add file, Add catalogue token, token Info/editing, diagram source, and other registered contributions on the mounted editor adapter; do not add a reduced subdoc editor.
  • [x] Preserve the existing parent request and response contract when sub_scope is absent.
  • [x] Cover exact request bodies, fixed target retention, contribution context, stale revision, rebuild failure, invalid target, and parent compatibility in focused service and browser-module tests.

SDE-2 implementation and evidence

  • docs-viewer-management-document-target.js is the only browser normalizer. Source entry supplies its exact target to the display-mode mount; the source editor freezes that target for read, rebuild, rendered refresh, Open in VS Code, diagram-source Info, and registered buffer contributions. Selection changes and the retired source=markdown URL entry no longer retarget or open the editor.
  • Source, diagram-source, import-result, and report-service clients send the normalized target directly. Parent reads retain scope and doc_id; only sub-scope reads and bodies add sub_scope. Payload fields cannot replace a normalized target.
  • docs_management_source_service.py and docs_diagram_source_service.py resolve parent and sub-scope requests through the shared server owner. Parent responses remain unchanged; sub-scope responses and activity add only sub_scope.
  • Sub-scope Save/Rebuild preserves the existing atomic source write, revision, timestamp, diagnostics, and activity behavior. It uses the configured sub-scope docs builder and the parent search builder, with a sub-scope-owned watcher suppression that prevents the live watcher from duplicating the completed rebuild.
  • Focused pytest over the target fixture/resolver, source and diagram services, rebuild and watcher helpers, management routes, sub-scope docs builder, search exclusion, and public runtime/service boundaries: 107 passed.
  • docs_viewer_catalogue_token_modules.py --site-root .: passed. It covered exact parent/sub-scope client and adapter requests, target override rejection, fixed-target source entry, successful rebuild, rebuild failure retention, stale captured ranges, and Catalogue contribution context.
  • docs_viewer_metadata_info_view_modules.py --site-root .: passed. Diagram discovery and open use the mounted sub-scope target without exposing a physical path.
  • docs_viewer_router_modules.py --site-root site: passed. It covered explicit provider/report-service targets and absence of the URL source-entry fallback. Its fixture server now maps the existing shared-site and repository-owned runtime boundaries required by that maintained smoke.
  • docs_viewer_service_manage.py: passed with an isolated, test-owned projects base. Its synthetic parent manage route covered the updated direct parent/sub-scope action-controller handoff only; it is not the integrated subdoc route evidence reserved for SDE-5.
  • Maintained explicit lint over the changed Python and JavaScript source/test files: passed. git diff --check: passed.

Checkpoint / review gate: demonstrate direct parent and sub-scope read/rebuild/open requests plus the fixed-target editor module. Review stale and failure recovery and all registered source-editor contributions before adding new toolbar controls.

[x] SDE-3 — Make Metadata Editing Target-Aware

  • [x] Supply Edit metadata with one explicit rendered target and load the full local source record through that target; do not hydrate editable state from a report manifest or compact by-ID payload.
  • [x] Extend metadata read and POST /docs/update-metadata through the shared resolver while preserving ordinary parent behavior.
  • [x] Render the sub-scope modal with Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and non-viewable, but without Parent or a hidden parent fallback.
  • [x] Omit parent_id from every sub-scope request and reject any sub-scope mutation that supplies it without writing.
  • [x] Rebuild only the targeted sub-scope detail and affected existing manifest/search projections. Preserve the local inventory and public eligibility behavior when viewable changes without exposing it publicly.
  • [x] Add planner/service tests for every editable field, no-op behavior, parent rejection, timestamp/revision behavior, non-viewable inclusion, public eligibility changes, and ordinary parent compatibility.
  • [x] Add modal/workflow tests proving full-record hydration, the exact sub-scope field set, and absence of displayed/selected-document fallback.

SDE-3 implementation and evidence

  • GET /docs/metadata and POST /docs/update-metadata normalize the same exact target and resolve it through docs_management_document_target.py. The read returns the editable source-backed record; it does not consult or widen generated public payloads.
  • Parent updates retain the existing record and rebuild behavior. A sub-scope update accepts Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and viewable, preserves existing parent_id and placement fields, omits Parent from its response/request field set, and rejects any supplied parent_id before a write or rebuild.
  • A sub-scope write uses the existing sub-scope atomic write/rebuild boundary. The focused visibility case changed an existing visible manifest row to ineligible, retained the rebuilt local by-ID payload and management inventory record, and kept manifest rows restricted to { doc_id, title }.
  • Metadata entry now calls openForTarget; the workflow loads through the local client, validates the returned target and identity, and retains that target until the modal settles. The selected document, displayed payload, URL parameters, and the retired loadManagedDocumentRecord path are not fallbacks.
  • Focused pytest over metadata planning/service, target resolution/read, management routes and service config, sub-scope docs, search exclusion, and public projection: 83 passed.
  • docs_viewer_modal_focus_modules.py --site-root .: passed. It covered the parent modal baseline and the exact enabled sub-scope field set with Parent hidden and disabled.
  • docs_viewer_service_manage.py: passed with test-owned payloads. It covered the local metadata-read fixture, exact parent/sub-scope client requests, target/identity validation, rejected target replacement, absence of a selected-document fallback, and local-origin protection. It is not the integrated subdoc route evidence reserved for SDE-5.
  • Maintained explicit lint over the thirteen changed Python and eight changed JavaScript source/test files: passed. git diff --check: passed.

Checkpoint / review gate: review one focused parent request and the complete sub-scope metadata matrix, including rejected parent_id, manage inventory refresh, and unchanged public schemas, before report and toolbar wiring.

[x] SDE-4 — Publish Validated Report State And Project Controls

  • [x] Add a narrow optional report-to-management callback or event that publishes a validated rendered subdoc target only after a listed by-ID detail has loaded successfully.
  • [x] Clear that target on list view, navigation start, unknown or unlisted subdoc, load failure, report unmount, and scope/document change.
  • [x] Keep the shared/public report runtime read-only. Consume the management inventory and render existing Status/non-viewable icons only when the manage host explicitly supplies it.
  • [x] Project the exact control-state matrix from this delivery: parent Source, subdoc Source, Edit metadata, and Return to doc across rendered list, rendered valid detail, invalid/loading detail, and Markdown source.
  • [x] Convert Source entry from a toggle to a one-way action. Keep both source entry controls visible but disabled in source mode and make Return to doc its only explicit toolbar exit.
  • [x] Route parent Source from the parent report target even while detail is displayed. Route subdoc Source and Edit metadata only from the validated management target; never infer either from report markup or URL parameters.
  • [x] Add pure control-projection and report-module tests for every state, public/manage inventory separation, accessible labels, and no dirty-editor target switching.

SDE-4 implementation and evidence

  • docs-subscope-report.js accepts optional manage-only inventory and state callbacks. It publishes a detail target only after list membership and by-ID payload identity succeed; list, detail navigation, invalid/error, document navigation, and report unmount clear it. Detail request generations prevent a stale response from republishing after Back or a newer document mount.
  • docs-viewer-management-document-reports.js reads the local inventory once, validates its collection identity, adds the existing Status/non-viewable icons and accessible row labels, and supplies the parent report target. The public caller supplies neither inventory nor callback and retains its manifest-only rows without either icon.
  • docs-viewer-management-report-controls.js projects Edit metadata, parent Source, subdoc Source, and Return to doc from explicit ordinary/report targets and rendered/loading/invalid/source state. Parent Source stays on the report document during valid detail; subdoc actions receive only the callback-validated child target.
  • Source is now a one-way entry action. In source mode both report Source controls remain visible and disabled, Return to doc is the sole explicit toolbar exit, and the fixed mounted editor target continues to own Open in VS Code and registered source contributions.
  • docs_viewer_subscope_report_modules.py --site-root .: passed. It covered the complete pure matrix, exact inventory request, navigation clearing, manage/public row separation, accessible icons, valid and mismatched by-ID identity, invalid IDs, stale detail suppression, unmount clearing, and the manage bridge's exact parent/child targets.
  • docs_viewer_service_manage.py: passed with its isolated, test-owned service data. It confirmed ordinary source entry is disabled in source mode, Return is enabled, and the existing management route returns through the new control.
  • docs_viewer_router_modules.py --site-root site, docs_viewer_catalogue_token_modules.py --site-root ., and docs_viewer_metadata_info_view_modules.py --site-root .: passed. These retained display-mode, fixed source-target contribution, and mounted Info contracts.
  • Maintained explicit lint over the eleven changed JavaScript and three changed Python source/test files: passed. The new module smoke is registered in the Docs Viewer smoke profile. git diff --check: passed.

Checkpoint / review gate: review the complete pure state matrix and mounted report module with no mutations. Confirm invalid/loading states remain disabled, public rendering remains unchanged, and each enabled control emits the exact target before integrated route work.

[ ] SDE-5 — Complete Return, Refresh, And Route Integration

  • [ ] Preserve scope, parent doc, and existing subdoc route parameters when entering source mode, opening/saving metadata, returning, or rebuilding.

  • [ ] Preserve current successful Save/Rebuild return behavior and recoverable stale-revision, service-unavailable, invalid-target, and rebuild-failure states.

Checkpoint / review gate: user acceptance of the manual UI, complete green evidence, current-state durable docs, and final diff review. Only then mark SDE-0 through SDE-6 complete and change ui_status from in-progress to done.

Completion And Evidence

  • Parent Source always reads the supplied parent report doc_id, even while a subdoc is displayed.
  • Subdoc Source is enabled only for a successfully displayed listed detail and sends the exact { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }.
  • The source editor has no selected/displayed-document fallback.
  • Edit metadata receives the parent target on report list view and the exact sub-scope target on a valid detail view, with no selected/displayed fallback.
  • The sub-scope modal contains every existing editable metadata field except Parent; its request contains no parent_id.
